anglelake.look: A wave of 7,500 blue-anodized aluminum panels rolls over the terminus; a cloud of acrylic discs shimmers.

beaconhill.look: Reached only by elevator, 160 feet down: glowing sea-creature forms drift beneath a cobalt ceiling.

bellevuedowntown.look: Terracotta-and-glass hub at the tunnel mouth by City Hall, a glowing 20-ft cyclorama drum overhead.

belred.look: Street-median platforms on Spring Blvd, a 460-ft hand-crafted stainless railing casting waterlike shadows.

capitolhill.look: Two pink-and-yellow Navy jets kiss over the deep platform; entrances glow with red murals and a green wall.

columbiacity.look: Twin garden-themed platforms in the MLK median, marked by a 35-foot bronze shovel cast with world plants.

downtownredmond.look: Elevated island platform above Cleveland Street, ringed by two dozen jewel-toned flat-glass mosaic murals.
downtownredmond.art: glass mosaic murals · six artists, Tieton Mosaic

eastmain.look: Low butterfly-roofed canopies beside Surrey Downs, a trackside lacework fence of mid-century motifs.

federalwaydowntown.look: The line's glassy southern terminus, dichroic fins arching over tall entrances in shifting rainbow light.

internationaldistrictchinatown.look: Open-air platforms below a red-trimmed plaza, its walls lined with folded stainless-steel origami panels.

judkinspark.look: Open-air platforms sunk in the I-90 trench, watched over by a 50-ft bronze-halftone teenage Hendrix.

kentdesmoines.look: Aerial hall spanning S 236th, steel canopy and glass clerestory glowing over tree-ring etched art glass.

lynnwoodcitycenter.look: Peach-canopied elevated terminus with blue towers and a 30-foot neon hummingbird glowing over the plaza.

marymoorvillage.look: Island platform and plaza at the park's edge; seed-like silver airships float in the garage atrium.

mercerisland.look: Glassy stacked pavilion wedged between I-90 lanes, suspended oars and boats recalling lake crossings.

mountbaker.look: Twin elevated platforms above Rainier Avenue, lit by Kemper's blown-glass sunrise of green and yellow.

mountlaketerrace.look: Treetop-height platform astride 236th St, wrapped in shifting lenticular forest panels in earth greens.

northgate.look: A thin cantilevered roof floats over the open-air platform; dragonfly wings shimmer across 100 feet of glass.

othello.look: Median platforms in NewHolly where cut-steel dancers whirl and a stacked totem balances a Creamsicle.

overlakevillage.look: Side platforms tight against SR 520, reached by a louvered bridge of green-phosphor pixel forest.

pioneersquare.look: A tall granite vault beneath the old city — gray at one end, pink at the other — hung with artifact clocks.

rainierbeach.look: A lone island platform on MLK where a brushed-aluminum dragonfly hovers and cabled pear halves recall orchards.

redmondtechnology.look: Center platform amid Microsoft's campus, under the white fabric peaks of an 1,100-ft canopied bridge.

roosevelt.look: Brick-and-glass headhouses, a restored neon radio sign, and a gold stepped pyramid over a daylit descent.

seatacairport.look: A 60-foot aerial island platform under steel trusses; stainless sails spin above the bridge to the terminal.

shorelinenorth185th.look: Open-air side platforms sunk in a trench beside I-5, where neon-green ferns of Octavia's Garden take root.

shorelinesouth148th.look: Elevated platform bookended by blue elevator towers and yellow kiosks, with bright-blue Flow cisterns below.

sodo.look: At-grade platforms on the old busway, gated by oversize rusted tools as warehouse murals slide past.

southbellevue.look: High island platform over Bellevue Way, 900 ft of gold-and-green hexagon panels echoing Mercer Slough.

springdistrict.look: Open trench platforms below brick-lined streets; a cut-metal dragon and phoenix span the walls.

stadium.look: A wide open-air island platform built for game-day crowds, in the shadow of Lumen Field and T-Mobile Park.

starlake.look: Low embankment platforms at the forest edge by I-5, wrapped in bright flower-printed glass panels.

symphony.look: Stainless steel and glass in high-tech lines, where the red LED glyphs of Electric Lascaux blink overhead.

tukwilainternationalblvd.look: A white winged roof atop a 51-foot hilltop platform, glass walls open to Mt. Baker and the airport tower.

udistrict.look: Black granite entries; orange and blue light tubes trace 85 feet down to a white corrugated vault.

universityofwashington.look: A glass wedge by Husky Stadium sinks 100 feet through a chamber of backlit geologic glyphs glowing aqua.

westlake.look: Carved terra-cotta vines and leaves spill down pale Art Deco stone, rooting Westlake Park into the tunnel.

wilburton.look: Tall guideway over I-405 with bold red canopies and a 40-ft mirrored X column that borrows the sky.
wilburton.art: “Four Corners Extruded” · Phillip K. Smith III
